content.title: Southern California Edison, others reach settlement to recover $2 billion tied to wildfires
content.summary: Out of the $2 billion, about $1.6 billion consists of uninsured claims and $400 million comprises of legal costs paid as of May 31 this year, the company's parent, Edison International, said on Friday.  The costs are primarily related to the Woolsey fire of 2018 that burned 96,949 acres of land in California, destroyed 1,643 structures, killed three people, and prompted the evacuation of more than 295,000 people.  Last year, the utility said it was seeking to recover $1.6 billion in losses related to the Thomas and Koenigstein fires which started in 2017 and the Montecito Mudslides of 2018, collectively known as TKM.
